meanings.note: мне кажется = I think, it seems to me

Кажется as a parenthetical word. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to seem', paired with 'показаться'.

examples.trans: I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.note: Indefinite adverb. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Even I feel a bit ashamed right now.
It became somehow quiet in the room.
For long? You need to convince me somehow!

meanings.note: Diminutive of ключ. Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'little key' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A small key to the cabinet.

meanings.note: Чн is pronounced шн. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'contact' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: All contacts go only through me.

examples.text: Будут разные провокации. Все контакты только через меня.
examples.trans: There will be various provocations. All contacts go only through me.

лежать.gloss: to lie, to be lying down

meanings.note: + на / в + prepositional. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to lie, to be lying down', paired with 'полежать'.

examples.trans: But I'll be lying next to Grishka for eternity.
The book is lying on the table.

examples.text: Телевизор мне смотреть недолго. А с Гришкой лежать вечность.
examples.trans: I won't be watching TV for much longer. But I'll be lying next to Grishka for eternity.
